summary: This note surveys unusual Waste-to-Energy (WtE) projects worldwide, mostly launched or progressed in 2023. Examples include a kinetic dance floor in San Francisco, coffee-ground biofuel in Stockholm, an algae facade in Hamburg, diaper recycling in Toronto, and pyrolysis of plastic bags and tires. It argues that creativity and technology are turning waste into valuable energy.
one_line: A roundup of inventive 2023 Waste-to-Energy projects worldwide that convert trash, from diapers to ocean debris, into power and fuel.
key_facts: Engineer Jamal Greene designed a kinetic dance floor in San Francisco, a pilot project launched on September 15, 2023, whose recycled tiles capture dancers' steps as electricity for the club's lights and sound systems.

Marianne Leclerc, a barista-turned-entrepreneur, had by October 2023 built a Stockholm startup that turns spent coffee grounds into biofuel for heating homes, powering machines and fueling transportation.
The BIQ House in Hamburg, unveiled in fall 2023 by architect Helena Strauss, has a facade of glass panels filled with algae that absorb CO2 and yield biomass harvested for biogas.

Linda and Raj Patel launched an initiative in Toronto in November 2023 that cleans and sorts used diapers, recycling the plastic and turning organic waste into fuel pellets for industrial power plants.
Professor Aya Sato and her team in Tokyo have worked since early 2023 on turning discarded paper into a carbon-rich material that captures sludge from wastewater and can then be burnt for energy.
In Lagos, engineer Chidi Okonkwo leads a pyrolysis facility that as of December 2023 turns thousands of tons of plastic bags into synthetic crude oil.
Scientist Maria Lopez and a multinational team operate vessels, which began operating in late September 2023, that skim ocean waste and process it onboard into clean-burning diesel.

Landfill gas, a mix of methane and carbon dioxide, was formerly burned off; energy companies like Harvest Power now capture it for electricity or natural gas, with initiatives appearing from mid-2023.
City engineer Neville Longbottom started a project in Bristol in September 2023 that extracts methane from wastewater treatment plants to power streetlights.
EcoTyre, founded by siblings Maria and Thomas Schmidt in Germany, uses pyrolysis to break down old tires into oil, gas and carbon char for industrial use.
